events.title: First Atoms Form
events.description: About 380,000 years after the Big Bang, the universe cools enough for neutral atoms to form.

events.title: First Stars
events.description: The first generations of stars ignite, beginning stellar production of heavier elements.

events.title: First Galaxies
events.description: Early galaxies assemble from stars, gas, and dark matter.

events.title: Solar System Forms
events.description: The Sun and planets begin forming from a collapsing cloud of gas and dust.

events.title: Earth Forms
events.description: Earth accretes from material orbiting the young Sun.

events.title: Moon Forms
events.description: A giant impact likely produces the debris that becomes the Moon.

events.title: Earliest Evidence of Life
events.description: Possible microbial traces indicate life emerged on Earth billions of years ago; exact timing is debated.

events.title: Oxygenic Photosynthesis Evolves
events.description: Cyanobacteria and their ancestors begin producing oxygen through photosynthesis.

events.title: Great Oxidation Event
events.description: Atmospheric oxygen rises substantially, transforming Earth chemistry.

events.title: Complex Cells Emerge
events.description: Eukaryotic cells with internal compartments arise during the Proterozoic.

events.title: Multicellular Life Expands
events.description: Complex multicellular organisms diversify over a long evolutionary interval.

events.title: Ediacaran Period Begins
events.description: The Ediacaran period marks the rise of distinctive large, soft-bodied organisms.

events.title: Cambrian Explosion
events.description: Animal diversity and recognizable body plans increase rapidly in the geological record.

events.title: Plants Colonize Land
events.description: Early land plants begin transforming terrestrial environments.

events.title: First Tetrapods
events.description: Vertebrates with limbs evolve from fish-like ancestors.

events.title: Permian Mass Extinction
events.description: Earth experiences its most severe known mass extinction.

events.title: Dinosaurs Emerge
events.description: The first dinosaurs appear in the Late Triassic.

events.title: Early Mammals
events.description: Early true mammals emerge during the Mesozoic Era.

events.title: Early Birds
events.description: Bird-like dinosaurs such as Archaeopteryx appear.

events.title: Flowering Plants Emerge
events.description: Angiosperms originate and later spread across terrestrial ecosystems.

events.title: Asteroid Impact and K–Pg Extinction
events.description: An impact and associated global changes eliminate non-avian dinosaurs and many other species.

events.title: Earliest Hominins
events.description: Early members of the human evolutionary lineage appear in Africa.

events.title: Earliest Known Stone Tools
events.description: Stone tools from Lomekwi, Kenya, predate the genus Homo.

events.title: Genus Homo Emerges
events.description: Early fossils attributed to Homo date to roughly 2.8 million years ago.

events.title: Early Humans Leave Africa
events.description: Early Homo populations expand into Eurasia.

events.title: Homo sapiens Emerges
events.description: Our species evolves in Africa approximately 300,000 years ago.

events.title: Major Human Dispersals
events.description: Homo sapiens populations spread widely beyond Africa over many millennia.

events.title: Figurative Cave Art Flourishes
events.description: Sophisticated cave paintings and portable art become prominent in the archaeological record.

events.title: End of the Last Ice Age Approaches
events.description: Late-glacial warming reshapes ecosystems and human environments.

events.title: Agricultural Revolution
events.description: Farming and animal domestication emerge in several regions over thousands of years.

events.title: Early Urban Civilizations
events.description: Increasingly complex urban societies develop in Mesopotamia.

events.title: The Wheel Develops
events.description: Wheeled vehicles appear in Eurasia around the fourth millennium BCE.

events.title: Writing Emerges
events.description: The earliest writing systems develop in Mesopotamia, followed by others elsewhere.

events.title: Unification of Ancient Egypt
events.description: Early dynastic rulers consolidate a unified Egyptian state.

events.title: Great Pyramid of Giza Built
events.description: Egyptian builders construct the Great Pyramid during the Fourth Dynasty.

events.title: Indus Valley Cities Flourish
events.description: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro form part of an extensive urban civilization.

events.title: Code of Hammurabi
events.description: Babylonian king Hammurabi issues a famous collection of laws.

events.title: Late Bronze Age Collapse
events.description: Major eastern Mediterranean states and trading systems destabilize.

events.title: Greek City-States Rise
events.description: Greek poleis expand in influence during the Archaic period.

events.title: Birth of Confucius
events.description: Confucius is traditionally dated to 551 BCE and becomes profoundly influential in Chinese thought.

events.title: Alexander Begins Persian Campaign
events.description: Alexander the Great launches his conquest of the Achaemenid Empire.

events.title: China Unified Under Qin
events.description: Qin Shi Huang unifies major warring states under the Qin dynasty.

events.title: Roman Empire Begins
events.description: Octavian receives the title Augustus, marking the start of imperial rule.

events.title: Common Era Year One
events.description: Year 1 CE begins the conventional Common Era numbering system; there is no year zero in this calendar.

events.title: Paper-Making Improved in China
events.description: Cai Lun is traditionally credited with improving paper-making methods.

events.title: Edict of Milan
events.description: Roman emperors Constantine and Licinius proclaim religious toleration.

events.title: Western Roman Empire Falls
events.description: Romulus Augustulus is deposed, a conventional marker for the end of the Western Roman Empire.

events.title: Beginning of Islamic Calendar
events.description: The Hijra, Muhammad’s migration to Medina, anchors the Islamic calendar; July 16 is the conventional epoch date.

events.title: Charlemagne Crowned Emperor
events.description: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne in Rome.

events.title: Battle of Hastings
events.description: William of Normandy defeats Harold II and subsequently conquers England.

events.title: Mongol Empire Founded
events.description: Temüjin becomes Genghis Khan and establishes the Mongol Empire.

events.title: Magna Carta Sealed
events.description: King John accepts a charter limiting royal power in certain respects.

events.title: Black Death Reaches Europe
events.description: Plague spreads across Europe, killing a very large share of its population.

events.title: European Printing Revolution
events.description: Gutenberg’s movable metal type printing methods transform book production.

events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.description: Ottoman forces capture Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Columbus Reaches the Caribbean
events.description: Columbus’s voyage initiates sustained transatlantic contact and European colonization.

events.title: Protestant Reformation Begins
events.description: Martin Luther’s Ninety-Five Theses become a symbol of the Reformation.

events.title: Copernicus Publishes Heliocentric Model
events.description: On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres argues for a Sun-centered planetary system.

events.title: Galileo Observes the Sky with a Telescope
events.description: Telescopic astronomy reveals new evidence about the Moon, planets, and stars.

events.title: Newton Publishes Principia
events.description: Newton describes laws of motion and universal gravitation.

events.title: Industrial Revolution Begins
events.description: Mechanized production and fossil-fuel-powered industry take off in Britain; timing is approximate.

events.title: U.S. Declaration of Independence
events.description: The Continental Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence.

events.title: French Revolution
events.description: The storming of the Bastille symbolizes a revolution in French political life.

events.title: First Smallpox Vaccination
events.description: Edward Jenner carries out his famous cowpox inoculation experiment.

events.title: Haiti Declares Independence
events.description: Haiti becomes an independent state after a successful revolution against slavery and colonial rule.

events.title: Darwin Publishes On the Origin of Species
events.description: Charles Darwin presents evolution by natural selection in a landmark book.

events.title: American Civil War Ends
events.description: Robert E. Lee surrenders at Appomattox, signaling the effective end of the American Civil War.

events.title: Periodic Table Published
events.description: Dmitri Mendeleev organizes chemical elements by recurring properties.

events.title: First Successful Telephone Call
events.description: Alexander Graham Bell and Thomas Watson demonstrate intelligible speech by telephone.

events.title: First Powered Airplane Flight
events.description: The Wright brothers achieve sustained controlled powered flight.

events.title: Einstein’s Annus Mirabilis
events.description: Albert Einstein publishes foundational papers on relativity, Brownian motion, and the photoelectric effect.

events.title: World War I Begins
events.description: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia as a European crisis escalates into global war.

events.title: Russian October Revolution
events.description: Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd (October 25 on the Julian calendar).

events.title: Influenza Pandemic
events.description: A devastating influenza pandemic spreads worldwide during 1918–1920.

events.title: Penicillin Discovered
events.description: Alexander Fleming observes the antibacterial effect of Penicillium mold.

events.title: Wall Street Crash
events.description: A major stock market crash accelerates a global economic crisis.

events.title: World War II Begins in Europe
events.description: Germany invades Poland, prompting Britain and France to declare war.

events.title: Atomic Bombing of Hiroshima
events.description: The United States drops an atomic bomb on Hiroshima, ushering in the nuclear age.

events.title: United Nations Founded
events.description: The UN Charter enters into force following World War II.

events.title: Partition and Independence of India
events.description: British India is partitioned into India and Pakistan amid mass displacement and violence.

events.title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
events.description: The UN General Assembly adopts a foundational global human rights declaration.

events.title: DNA Double Helix Described
events.description: Watson and Crick publish a model of DNA structure informed by key experimental work.

events.title: Sputnik 1 Launched
events.description: The Soviet Union launches the first artificial Earth satellite.

events.title: First Moon Landing
events.description: Apollo 11 astronauts land on the Moon.

events.title: Berlin Wall Opens
events.description: Border crossings open, symbolizing the collapse of communist regimes in Eastern Europe.

events.title: World Wide Web Goes Public
events.description: Tim Berners-Lee announces the World Wide Web project publicly.

events.title: Soviet Union Dissolves
events.description: The Soviet Union formally ceases to exist.

events.title: September 11 Attacks
events.description: Coordinated terrorist attacks kill nearly 3,000 people in the United States.

events.title: Human Genome Project Completed
events.description: The international project announces completion of its reference human genome sequencing effort.

events.title: iPhone Introduced
events.description: Apple unveils the iPhone, accelerating the smartphone era.

events.title: Global Financial Crisis Intensifies
events.description: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy amid a worldwide financial emergency.

events.title: Higgs Boson Discovery Announced
events.description: CERN researchers announce evidence for a Higgs boson.

events.title: Paris Climate Agreement Adopted
events.description: Countries adopt a global agreement on climate change.

events.title: COVID-19 Declared a Pandemic
events.description: The World Health Organization characterizes COVID-19 as a pandemic.

events.title: Russia Invades Ukraine
events.description: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

events.title: ChatGPT Released
events.description: OpenAI publicly releases ChatGPT, accelerating public adoption of generative AI.

events.title: Israel–Hamas War Begins
events.description: Hamas-led attacks on Israel are followed by a devastating war in Gaza.

events.title: First Samples Returned from Moon’s Far Side
events.description: China’s Chang’e 6 mission returns the first samples collected from the lunar far side.

events.title: Present Day
events.description: The timeline reaches October 25, 2026; this is a timeline endpoint, not a historical discovery.
